meta.description: Parsa Derakhshan is a full-stack developer in Ottawa, building the Canadian Coast Guard's internal web applications in C#, .NET and Vue.

intro.p1: Since January 2022 I've been a programmer analyst at the Canadian Coast Guard, which moved from Fisheries and Oceans Canada to National Defence in September 2025. I build the internal web applications its staff rely on, mostly in C#/.NET and Vue, on SQL Server and Oracle.
intro.p2: Before that I was a data analyst intern at the Canadian Food Inspection Agency, and I studied Computer Engineering Technology at Algonquin College.

intro.photoCaption: On the Ottawa River, Parliament Hill behind me.

inkplusbot.title: InkPlusBot
inkplusbot.meta: 2024 to now · C#, EF Core, PostgreSQL, Redis, Docker
inkplusbot.body: A customer-facing Telegram bot for INK+, an Ottawa electronics repair and printing shop with three locations. It speaks English, French and Persian, finds ink and toner, gives repair estimates, lists refurbished devices and hands people over to staff. Product data comes from the INK+ website, which syncs from Lightspeed Retail. It runs in Docker on Linux, with Redis for conversation state and PostgreSQL for requests.

skiPatrol.title: Canadian Ski Patrol member system
skiPatrol.meta: 2023, college capstone · Java, Spring Boot, Hilla, Lit
skiPatrol.body: A college capstone that replaced the Canadian Ski Patrol's old Laravel/PHP member system, built for them as a real client. It has modules for events, training history, HR records and financial reports, each with a Java entity, a typed Hilla endpoint and a Lit view, and the interface is fully bilingual. It was handed to the Ski Patrol's contact, who deployed it to production.

experience.title: Experience

items.org: Canadian Coast Guard (Fisheries and Oceans Canada, now National Defence)
items.body: I designed the back end of ATONIS, the system that tracks Canada's buoys and other aids to navigation: a .NET 8 API using CQRS, an Entity Framework model that follows the IHO S-201 standard, and a GraphQL API that answers map questions (what is inside this area, what is near this point) and exports GeoJSON. On the front end I built its Vue and Leaflet map, where staff draw and edit areas directly. I also moved FS3 to a new Azure DevOps project with rebuilt pipelines, started bringing the 2007-era Fleet Safety System onto Razor Pages, and work on iPlan, the Pay Issue Portal, NTTT, PMIS and Activity Based Budgeting. Tests run from xUnit unit tests through integration tests against a real SQL Server to Selenium.

Wrote and tested Python scripts that automate the agency's yearly data update, built Power BI dashboards and analysis tools for researchers, and helped update the Comparative Risk Model with data gathered alongside Statistics Canada and other agencies.
Built the research group's website from the first design, working from what they asked for, then maintained the site and its database and added pages as needed, with every change tracked in Git.

rag.title: Private search over my immigration paperwork
rag.meta: 2026 · Swift (Apple Vision), Python, SQLite FTS5, pikepdf
rag.body: The retrieval half of a RAG system over my own IRCC files: 745 scans, photos, passport stamps, letters and fillable government forms, in English and Persian. Each file is read the best way it can be: PDF text, OCR through Apple Vision, or the typed answers inside IRCC's fillable forms. Every page then goes into a SQLite full-text index. Persian digits and spellings are normalized, and a date in any format also finds its other forms, including the Persian calendar. Rebuilds only re-read files that changed.
rag.eval: To know whether it works, a test set checks 31 key facts, such as permit numbers, dates and stamps, and a fact only counts when it is found in the file it should come from. It finds 30. Everything runs on my Mac and nothing is sent anywhere. Next is the answer layer, which will cite the exact page behind every claim.

scout.title: Scout: reading used-computer ads with Claude
scout.meta: 2026 · C#, .NET 10, Anthropic SDK, Claude Haiku, PostgreSQL
scout.body: Scout works out what used laptops, tablets and desktops really sell for around Ottawa. Claude Haiku reads every Marketplace, Kijiji, eBay and store listing once, and again only if its text changes, and answers in JSON against a fixed schema: what kind of ad it is, then brand, family, exact model, configuration and condition. The prompt lists the products already known so the same machine always gets the same name, and that part is cached across requests. Ads go 20 to a request, 4 requests at a time, and the status page tracks the cost: about ten cents per thousand listings. The prompt and the parsing of answers are plain functions with unit tests, so they are tested without calling the model.
scout.caption: From ReaderPrompt.cs: part of the instructions that keep model names consistent.

tools.title: Working with Claude Code
tools.body: I build with Claude Code and give it project rules it can't skip. For the INK+ website I wrote a /vibe-check skill that screenshots a page at phone and desktop sizes and audits it against our design rules, plus hooks that check every edit against the design and copy rules and block any commit that stages a secret file. This site went through the same checklist.
